Order
This is a petition filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. seeking quashing of the FIR/Crime No.49/2023 registered under Section 376(2)(n) of the IPC at the Police Station, Mahila Thana,
District Betul and ensued proceedings thereon.
2. The counsel for the petitioner contends that the prosecutrix in the present case has lodged the impugned FIR against the petitioner.

As per the said FIR, the present petitioner under the garb of false promise of marriage, entered in forcible sexual intercourse relations with the prosecutrix and accordingly committed the offence of rape.
It is contended by the counsel that the impugned FIR and the ensued proceedings thereon, are unsustainable inasmuch as the prosecutrix is undisputedly a major woman.
The relationship between the prosecutrix and the present petitioner was consensual and there was no misconception of facts.

It is contended by the counsel that if there is failure to adhere to the promise made at a previous NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12435 2 MCRC-8782-2024 point of time, the same cannot be brought within the ambit of "false promise".
This aspect has already been taken into consideration in catena of decisions.
3. It is contended by the counsel for the petitioner that apparently the report has been lodged as an afterthought and with oblique motive to falsely implicate the present petitioner.

The report is conspicuously silent as regards the specific instances on which the offence of rape was committed by Harshit Nagle vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197386837/
1 the present petitioner.

sentences.text: The report has been lodged on 27-12-2023 and in the report the specific date of commission of offence is shown as 04-11-2022.
There are no details of any other dates after 04-11-2022.
Hence, apparently there is no explanation of delay in lodging the FIR of more than one year.

sentences.text:
The counsel for the State has opposed the prayer and submitted that the present petition seeking quashment of the FIR and ensued proceedings thereon, by the petitioner, being sans substance,
deserves to be dismissed.

5 . Having considered the submissions, perusal of the records as well as FIR reflects, that the prosecutrix has levelled the allegations that the present petitioner got acquainted with the prosecutrix through Instagram.

Thereafter, he assured the prosecutrix that he would enter into wedlock with her and then while making false promise of marriage, the offence of rape was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12435 3 MCRC-8782-2024 committed by the present petitioner.
The FIR, thus, prima facie reflects that the allegations pertaining to commission of offence and as such quashment of the same at this stage, is premature.
Thus, this Court refrains itself from interfering with the FIR and ensued proceedings thereon.
6. Interference with the FIR and ensuing proceedings thereon, is not permissible.

Even otherwise,
such record is not available with the Court while exercising powers conferred under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, as this Court cannot conduct mini trials in exercise of inherent powers, no interference with the FIR is warranted.

[Please see : Criminal Appeal No. 330/2021 (M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Private Limited Vs. State of Maharashtra) decided on 13th April, 2021 reported in AIR (SC) (CRI)-2021-0-1093].
7.

8. Consequently, the instant petition stands dismissed.
